subject: physics_2
question_text: What is the principle of superposition?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. Physics hand-checked: when two or more waves act on the same particle at the same time, the resultant displacement equals the ALGEBRAIC sum of the individual displacements, y = y₁ + y₂ + … + yₙ — the word algebraic (signs included) is what makes both constructive and destructive interference follow from the one statement.

recall_prompt: Say the principle of superposition — the statement and the equation.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The statement
lines: When two or more waves act on a particle
of the medium at the same time, the
resultant displacement of the particle is
the algebraic sum of the individual
steps.margin_note: First mark. The word algebraic is part of the statement — signs are included in the sum.
steps.why: Algebraic means the displacements add WITH their signs. That one word is why two waves can cancel (opposite signs) as well as reinforce (same signs) — both interference cases come from this single sentence.
common_mistakes: Writing sum without algebraic — a plain sum could not describe two waves cancelling.
Adding amplitudes instead of displacements — the principle adds the instantaneous displacements at one particle.

recall.must_convey: That the resultant displacement is the algebraic sum of the displacements the individual waves would each produce.
accept: resultant displacement is the algebraic sum
waves acting together add their displacements
reject: y equals y one plus y two

steps.memory_tip: One particle, many waves: add what each wave alone would do, signs and all.

steps.label: The equation
lines: For n waves with displacements y₁, y₂, …
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the sum out to yₙ so it reads for ANY number of waves.
steps.why: The equation is the statement in symbols: each yᵢ is the displacement wave i alone would give the particle at that instant, and the particle actually shows their sum.
common_mistakes: Stopping at y = y₁ + y₂ — the principle holds for any number of waves, so write the sum to yₙ.

recall.must_convey: That the equation is y equals y one plus y two up to y n.
accept: y equals y1 plus y2 and so on
sum of all the individual displacements

steps.memory_tip: Statement in words, then the same statement in symbols — the equation is not extra content.

insider_note: The word algebraic carries the first mark; writing the sum out to yₙ (not stopping at two waves) protects the second.
